summary: Backend-only testing for HappyHour MVP (first iteration). Created pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_happyhour_api.py with 26 test cases covering categories, merchants, deals (filters, sorts, live-now, reels), auth (register/login/me/patch), follow toggle, and claim lifecycle (claim + quantity decrement + cancel + restore). All 26 tests passed against the public URL https://local-deals-now.preview.emergentagent.com. Auto-seed produced the expected 6 merchants + 15 deals near lat=37.7749, lng=-122.4194. No MongoDB _id leaks in any response; passwords hidden on /auth/me; JWT auth (HS256, 30d) works; quantity decrement is atomic and cancel restores; redemption_code is 6 chars and qr_payload starts with 'HH:'.

minor.issue: Startup event uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup')/'shutdown'; still functional but Starlette recommends the lifespan handler (see server.py:706, 742).

Sort applied only when lat is not None (server.py:313). When only lat/lng missing and sort='distance' is requested, response silently falls back to the default heuristic. Consider returning 400 or documenting behaviour.
When the deal's merchant_id is missing/invalid, response contains 'merchant': null. Guard for that case is fine but not documented.

action_items: (Optional) Migrate startup/shutdown to FastAPI lifespan context manager to remove deprecation warnings.
(Optional) Return 400 when sort=distance is requested without lat/lng, instead of silently ignoring.
critical_code_review_comments: Emails are correctly lowercased on register/login — tests must lowercase before comparison.
Password hash is stripped via projection in get_current_user and update_me — good.
Atomic quantity decrement via update_one with quantity_remaining > 0 guard — race-safe, verified by decrement + restore test.
All Mongo reads use projection {'_id': 0} — no ObjectId leaks confirmed by recursive assertion in tests.
server.py is 745 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline; consider splitting into routers (auth, merchants, deals, claims, seed) as feature grows.
seed_data_creation: None manually created; backend auto-seeded 6 merchants + 15 deals on startup. Test-created users use 'test_<uuid>@happyhour.io' emails and claims are created + cancelled in-place (not fully cleaned up but isolated per run).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green. Test suite at /app/backend/tests/test_happyhour_api.py can be reused as regression. Base URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. For next iteration, frontend Expo web preview at localhost:3000 should be tested for onboarding → browse (deals grid, map, reels) → auth (register/login) → claim → my claims → cancel → follow merchant flows.
